synthesis: The Scout Map order-density layers (Direct + Staging) should exclude hotlist addresses whose plate is too short to be a real, actionable plate, matching the dashboard-stats rule. The ticket frames it as 'add a >= 3 guard', but the order query already carries a stricter `length(plate) > 3` guard; the real change is to relax `> 3` to `>= 3` so the order map matches HotlistCount (dashboard stats), which uses `>= 3`.

scope.summary: REVISED: hardcode the plate-length guard in HotlistAddressGeohashQuery from `> 3` to `>= 3` (one line). One query serves Direct (staging=false), Staging (staging=true), AND the non-Scout KitUserPathController heatmap; all three now use `>= 3`, matching dashboard stats. No caller edits and no param — Dalton chose to drop the param as over-engineered (q2 revised).

proposed_changes.change: line ~150: `AND length(plate) > 3` -> `AND length(plate) >= 3` (+ a 2-line explanatory comment).
proposed_changes.reason: Match the dashboard-stats `>= 3` rule (HotlistCount.php:74-76) on the order-map density layers.

acceptance_criteria.reason: HotlistCount.php uses `length(plate) >= 3`; the edit makes the order query identical.

questions.q: q1: The order query is HotlistAddressGeohashQuery, whose plate guard is currently `> 3` (not absent). Confirm the intended end state is `>= 3` (relax, keeps length-3 plates), matching dashboard stats — i.e. this is a change, not an addition?
questions.answer: >= 3 (relax, per ticket) — the AC 'matches dashboard-stats >= 3 rule' is the target end state.

questions.q: q2: HotlistAddressGeohashQuery is also called by KitUserPathController (the non-Scout repo user-path heatmap). Editing the shared query relaxes its guard to `>= 3` too. OK to apply uniformly to all callers (simplest, one edit, consistent), or keep KitUserPathController on `> 3`?
questions.answer: REVISED 2026-07-13: hardcode `>= 3` in the shared query for ALL callers (drop the min_plate_length param). KitUserPathController repo heatmap also moves to `>= 3` — accepted (marginal: only exactly-length-3 plates). Dalton judged the param over-engineered for a value that never varies. Supersedes the initial 'Scout-only via param' answer.

questions.q: q3: DEV-2163 set ScoutCheckInRollupQuery to `> 3` explicitly to match the order query. Moving the order query to `>= 3` re-introduces a check-in-vs-order-map divergence. Leave check-in rollup (and the dashboard-controller queries) on `> 3` as out-of-scope, or align them too?
questions.answer: Keep narrow — order query only. Leave ScoutCheckInRollupQuery + ClarityScoutDashboardController on `> 3`; flag the new divergence as a follow-up.

notes: Change is a one-line SQL relaxation; the query is unchanged otherwise.

The guard is inside a `clarity.hotlist FINAL` subquery filtering hotlist_id membership; plate lives on clarity.hotlist. `length()` on a Nullable plate returns 0 for NULL in ClickHouse, so `< 3` short/NULL plates are excluded either way; only the exactly-length-3 boundary moves.

tests.what_it_pins: A hotlist row with a length-3 plate now contributes an address geohash cell to both direct and staging layers; a length-2 plate does not.
